narrative.overview: Séance-fork is a spirit companion that watches your agents and knocks when one needs you. The interface is the quiet room; the terminals are the summoned. Chrome stays still and Adwaita-true while the state of each agent surfaces through small, precise signals: a symbolic icon, an unread dot, a 2px outline, a knock-blue flash. By default the chrome is simply the OS system theme — stock libadwaita, light or dark, tracked live. The defining mechanism is opt-in possession: set a ghostty theme and every chrome color is re-derived from the terminal palette; unset it and the window returns to stock Adwaita. Depth is tonal, never shadowed; state is outlined, never recolored.
keyCharacteristics: System theme by default: stock libadwaita chrome following the OS light/dark preference
Opt-in palette possession: setting a ghostty theme re-derives every chrome color from the terminal palette
Flat surfaces; depth comes from fg/bg mixes at 4–15%, never from shadows
State carried by 2px outlines and symbolic icons, not by status hues
One accent (ANSI blue), one notification color (ANSI bright blue)
Adwaita-native controls, symbolic icons, system typography
Motion is short and functional: 100–200ms ease-in-out, 150ms revealers

rules.name: The Palette Is the Chrome Rule
rules.body: Never hardcode a chrome color. In the default state, reference libadwaita's named colors and let the OS theme resolve them; in the possessed state, the same named colors resolve from the terminal palette.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Agent status never gets its own hue. Working, idle, and needs-input are distinguished by symbolic icon and outline, not by green/yellow/red.

rules.name: The Dim Label Rule
rules.body: Secondary information is the primary ink at reduced opacity (0.8 / 0.6 / 0.5), never a second text color and never smaller than 8px.

rules.name: The Two Fonts Rule
rules.body: The app has exactly two fonts: the system UI font for chrome (fixed, unconfigurable) and the terminal font for cell content (user-configurable in Settings). Font settings never cross the boundary in either direction.

rules.name: The Outline Carries State Rule
rules.body: Focus, notification, flash, and drop-target are 2px outlines at −2px offset. Shadows are for overlays and drag physics only — never for resting surfaces.

rules.name: The Backdrop Dim Rule
rules.body: When the window loses focus, sidebar chrome dims to 50% opacity over 200ms; accent-colored selection stays lit.

dos: Do resolve every new chrome color from @window_bg_color / @window_fg_color (or a documented 4–15% mix), the accent, or the notify token
Do use symbolic (*-symbolic) icons exclusively; tint with color, size via icon-size or px
Do express state as 2px outlines at −2px offset and symbolic-icon swaps, keeping layout stable
Do keep secondary text as the primary ink at 0.8/0.6/0.5 opacity
Do use stock libadwaita patterns (AdwDialog, AdwPreferencesPage, .boxed-list, .dim-label, .title-4) for dialogs
Do swap theme CSS atomically: attach the new provider before detaching the old
donts: Don't add status hues — no @success_color/@warning_color/@error_color in chrome; .destructive-action in settings dialogs is the sole exception
Don't add resting shadows or card-style elevation; the command palette shadow is a deliberate singleton
Don't style chrome toward one fixed palette; the default state must stay correct under stock libadwaita, light and dark
Don't let the terminal font setting leak into chrome, or add an app-font setting — The Two Fonts Rule; nothing in chrome exceeds 14px
Don't use Knock Blue (#51a1ff) decoratively — it means a pane needs you
Don't give workspace color codes any status meaning; they are user-assigned identity tags
Don't introduce GTK3 idioms or non-symbolic icons in new UI
